line: And when you see me, just acknowledge the G
vault_lines: And when you see me, just acknowledge the G
meaning: G is a double entendre for G as in gangster and G in his name G Herbo. He asking for acknowledgement and respect when in his presence.

line: We facin’ the pressure of family that we watched suffer I gotta lift ’em up out of the gutter I make a check and send that to my mother They root for me like Ireland and Conor McGregor
vault_lines: We facin' the pressure of family that we watched suffer
meaning: Saba speaks out about how when a family member gets rich, their family always will ask for some money. He feels the pressure on him from his family who are still stuck in Chicago asking for help. He than compares himself by saying his family and others in Chicago cheer him on like how Ireland does with Connor McGregor, a professional UFC fighter from Ireland

line: ‘Cause some people didn’t make it doin’ life
vault_lines: 'Cause some people didn't make it doin' life
meaning: This double entendre talks about how those who don’t get successful are forced into working their entire lives to make enough money to live or live a life of crime that can end them up in prison.

line: Even in the wintertime they identifyin’ all these niggas dyin’ Ain’t no breakin’ time for the bacon, swine
vault_lines: Even in the wintertime they identifyin' all these niggas dyin'
meaning: Saba tells us that in the city there are no breaks in violent crimes. He elaborates on this by saying that due to the amount of crime there are no breaks for “the bacon, swine”. Bacon and swine both refer to a pig which is the common nickname given to law enforcement. In a city so deep in crime, there is no rest for the police.

line: Raise the mortgage higher I’m stand my ground like a fuckin’ squatter
vault_lines: I'm stand my ground like a fuckin' squatter
meaning: Squatters are known for moving into people’s homes and refusing to pay rent or leave, ultimately ‘standing their ground’ to the law and the individual. Regardless of the price, they’re going to always be a step ahead and take what you have standing their ground.

line: This came until my mother say ”How would you like to come to Chicago and work for me? And if you don’t like it, I send you train fare to come back”
vault_lines: This came until my mother say "How would you like to come to Chicago and work for me?
meaning:
The album for me acts kind of like a generational dialogue. As I was writing a lot of the songs and thinking of the stories that I wanted to share—before I even thought of the concept to involve my grandfather—he’s somebody who I was thinking of. My grandparents in general—because as I’m getting older and as I’m experiencing more things and more life, I’m realizing a lot of things that I’m experiencing now, they experienced in the 60s and 70s, in very different ways than what’s happening right now. I wanted to talk to him and learn from him and just give perspective. We started having open discussions, and I told him I wanted to interview him and learn some of our family’s history. I don’t want to take that for granted while I got them here. I want to get as much information out of them as I can.

He’s from Houston, Texas. In that clip [at the end of “Survivor’s Guilt”], he’s referring to a woman who was in Chicago, who was hiring his mom. And she told his mom that she would give her a train fare to go back if she didn’t like Chicago. That’s how my family ended up in Chicago in the first place. I thought it was important to include that, based on how much of our roots are in Chicago—it was cool to get the story of how we even got there.


– Saba, Chicago Reader

line: I’m tryna move better, what’s really eatin’ when you from a food desert?
vault_lines: I'm tryna move better, what's really eatin' when you from a food desert?
meaning:
This is a pun: all my n***** eating is a whole trope, he’s suggesting none of them are ‘eating’ because they live in a food desert.

Food Desert (Wikipedia): A food desert is an area that has limited access to affordable and nutritious food, in contrast with an area with higher access to supermarkets or vegetable shops with fresh foods, which is called a food oasis. The designation considers the type and quality of food available to the population, in addition to the accessibility of the food through the size and proximity of the food stores.

In 2010, the United States Department of Agriculture reported that 23.5 million people in the U.S. live in “food deserts”, meaning that they live in low income census tracts more than one mile from a supermarket in urban or suburban areas and more than 10 miles from a supermarket in rural areas.

line: My father told me that the world was mine and I believed him
vault_lines: My father told me that the world was mine and I believed him
meaning:
Saba’s father, Chandlar, has been a large supporter of him. He has showed up various times in Saba’s music, such as being a backup singer on the artist’s NPR Tiny Desk Concert, and as a feature on Saba’s songs  “United Center” (2014) and “GPS” (2016).

Like Saba, Chandlar pursued a music career, but did not reach the level of success that Saba has, which is discussed in Saba’s 2018 song “Fighter:”

Or, shit, at least in the army, instead you chose to hip-hopper
I know how this is gon' end ‘cause I went through this with your father

line: Bitch, I was rich at twenty-one And I’m still on savage shit like 21
vault_lines: Bitch, I was rich at twenty-one
meaning:
While reminiscing on the first years and successes of his career, which include his breakout mixtape Welcome to Fazoland (2014), his inclusion in the XXL Freshman Class (2016) and his debut album Humble Beast (2017), G Herbo also makes a reference to the Atlanta-based rapper, 21 Savage.



Herbo and Savage have collaborated on three tracks: “How I Grew Up” (2018), “By Any Means” (2020) and “T.O.P.” (2021). Plus, they were featured together on the official remix of Nardo Wick’s 2021 song “Who Want Smoke??”.

line: Ayy, ayy, ayy, raised below poverty Now I keep it sacred geometry, I’m with my circle I’m trainin’ for mayhem, but y’all on more triangle ’Cause I saw silly niggas done change up I’m still on my square like a Plaintiff Be careful, they armed and they dangerous For diamonds some niggas is spirallin’ They want us in boxes, but can’t contain us, oh my God
vault_lines: Ayy, ayy, ayy, raised below poverty
meaning:
Saba uses clever wordplay to exaggerate the way immature people don’t change.

He mentions triangles, then saying, “I saw silly,” sounding like he says “isosceles,” a type of triangle that has two sides of equal length.



He continues the geometrical theme by mentioning squres to say how he still keeps things true to himself. He makes a reference to Oakley Plaintiff Squared Sunglasses.



He then finishes off the geometrical theme by saying that he’s too good to be boxed in or “contained” by the people trying to put him down.

line: My grandpa smilin’ with no teeth in, my cousin still supposed to be h-
vault_lines: My grandpa smilin' with no teeth in, my cousin still supposed to be h-
meaning:
Once more, Saba pays homage to his cousin Walter Long Jr., one of the founding members of Pivot Gang and also known as dinnerwithjohn and John Walt. Walter was fatally stabbed during an altercation he had after he got off a train on February 9, 2017.

Walt’s death and legacy was a recurring topic of Saba’s 2018 album CARE FOR ME, and some of the songs were dedicated solely to him, such as “PROM/KING” and “HEAVEN ALL AROUND ME.”

Saba has also mentioned his late cousin on other songs, such as “Beautiful Smile” (2018):

I got a beautiful smile, honestly I forgot how
Since I put my boy in a box, sometime I see him in the cloud

And “Areyoudown? Pt. 2” (2020):

Granny left too soon, if only she could see me now
Walt right off 2-90, I might go and see him now
